title: The Mesnevi, Book 1
author: Jalal al-Din Rumi (Redhouse trans)
description: The Mesnevi of Mevlana (Our Lord) Jelalu-'d-Din Muhammed er-Rumi, Book the First, translated and poetised by James W. Redhouse (London: Trübner, 1881), together with selections from the Acts of the Adepts (Manaqib al-Arifin) of Aflaki, giving the life and anecdotes of Rumi and his circle. Redhouse, the celebrated Ottoman lexicographer, rendered the first book of Rumi's great Persian mystical poem into English rhyming verse. The Mathnawi, called the 'Qur'an in Persian', opens with the song of the reed flute lamenting separation from its reed bed, symbol of the soul's longing for God, and unfolds through interwoven stories, parables and teachings: the king and the handmaid, the grocer and the parrot, the lion and the hare, Moses and the shepherd and many others. Redhouse's version was one of the first substantial English translations of Rumi.
